A short that has gone 109.8m to 127-143m shares and 2.4 to ~5.7 days to cover since July, call-heavy OI, six of eight prints up, and the Blade earn-out 8-K pointing to a Q3 revenue beat in its seasonal peak; the Dubai/first-passenger slip risk is an absence rather than a document and the two GAAP one-offs (verdict accrual, warrant mark) offset each other.

The strongest name in the pack: the Westerman target's ~$160m 2025 revenue sits in the Recent Developments block of a 424B5 for an unnamed target and is not in the reaffirmed $450-500m guide or the $470.6m Street, and the three Q3 LEU/HALEU prepayment contracts have undisclosed values that only the 10-Q can put into backlog and customer advances - both land on guidance into a 29.7%-short, 6.8-day-to-cover stock at its 52-week low with balanced skew; capped by a seasonally light quarter, a disputed EPS bar and the undisclosed DOE backlog treatment.

Sanofi's own Q3 (flu/COVID -18.8% CER, NH deliveries phased to Q4) and Pfizer's US Comirnaty -35% both land on the unguided Sanofi royalty/supply line that is excluded from Novavax's framework, but the bar is disputed ($50.6m to $78.7m, one source cut 22.5%), the phasing reverses next quarter, and a 28.7% short with six of eight prints up plus the $125m CIC milestone to frame on the call pull it most of the way back to zero.
